text:
Maria Chen: Heads-up — ran the GPU capability probe across a sample of H100 and A100 nodes overnight. Seeing inconsistent FP8/BF16 capability flags reported by the vendor driver in some containers.
Josh Patel: Ugh. Which flag specifically?
Maria Chen: On a few hosts the probe reports `bf16_supported=true` but our kernel chooser later falls back to a slower FP32 path. Suspect mismatch in the runtime detection vs. driver query.
Devon King: Can you paste the probe output for one of the failing hosts?
Maria Chen: Sure — here's the trimmed output from the failing H100:
```
# /opt/redwood/bin/gpu-cap-probe --json
{"gpu":"NVIDIA H100-PCIe","sm":90,"tensor_cores":true,"bf16":true,"fp8":false,"driver":535.113}
```
Samir Rao: And the runtime kernel selector log for the same request?
Maria Chen: From runtime debug at request time: `kernel_path=attn_bf16_fallback -> selected=attn_fp32_kernel_v2`
Liam O'Neill: So runtime thought it couldn't run bf16, even though probe said bf16=true. Means either (a) probe ran in different LD_LIBRARY_PATH/container, or (b) we check capabilities at model load time and override later.
Anya Singh: Could also be the cuda driver vs. cuDNN/cutlass ABI mismatch. We saw similar w/ tensorcore heuristics before.
Josh Patel: Did you check compute capability (SM) mapping? Maybe our SM->kernel table doesn't include 90/91 properly.
Maria Chen: Probe records `sm=90`. Our kernel table maps 80->ampere_v2, 90->hopper_v1 but the kernel honcho has a special-case for `sm>=90 && driver<536` to avoid fp8 path. That clause was introduced in 176xxx PR.
Devon King: That sounds like the regression. Which hosts had driver < 536?
Maria Chen: A mix — some cloud images ship 535.x but concat with vendor libs yields fp8=false.
Infra Bot: NOTE: 3 hosts in us-west2-rtpool are on driver 535.113, affected by kernel-fallback rule. Incident created: INC-2026-0412.
Samir Rao: Ok, short-term: can we change the detection to prefer runtime probe at container startup (cudaDeviceGetAttribute) rather than relying solely on install-time probe?
Maria Chen: I prototyped a small probe that calls `cudaDeviceGetAttribute(cudaDevAttrComputeCapabilityMajor, &maj)` and also queries cutlass/torch backend for `supports_bf16`. Rough output: 
```
cuda_major=9, cuda_minor=0
cutlass_bf16=true
torch_backend_bf16=false (container torch 2.2 compiled without bf16)
```
Anya Singh: There you go — container-level libs differ. Runtime kernel selection should combine driver-level SM info + library-level bf16 availability.
Josh Patel: For autotuning: we also need sequence-length dependent paths. We saw long seqs (2048+) prefer a different matmul tiling; the chooser currently bases on SM only.
Devon King: Suggestion: update kernel selector to evaluate triple key: (sm_family, bf16_available_in_container, max_seq_bucket). If bf16 missing in container, mark kernels that require cutlass bf16 as disabled even if GPU advertises it.
Liam O'Neill: Agree. We can add a fast cache: container_probe_hash -> enabled_kernels set. Invalidate on lib reload or when we detect PyTorch/TF process start.
Samir Rao: Also add a telemetry gauge so we can see counts of fallback events by node/driver/kernel. That will help detect regressions early.
Maria Chen: I ran perf microbench: same model, same node, two containers. When bf16 kernels were disabled, token throughput dropped 2.6x for seq>=1024. Profile snippet: 
```
seq=128: 1.1k tokens/s (no change)
seq=1024: bf16_path=2.6k tok/s, fp32_path=980 tok/s
KV cache memcpy spike on fp32 path: +18ms per request
```
Josh Patel: That's huge. KV memcpy suggests kernel layout mismatch; maybe bf16 kernels use packed kv layout. If runtime falls back to fp32, it still expects packed layout and ends up memcpy'ing a conversion.
Anya Singh: We should make layout conversion explicit at module boundary, not implicit in kernel. Avoid hidden assumptions.
Devon King: Action items: (1) Maria to open PR that changes probe precedence + adds container lib checks (2) Liam to add cache keyed by container probe hash (3) Samir to add telemetry counter for kernel fallbacks (4) Josh to add test fixture that simulates driver 535 + lib mismatch.
Maria Chen: I'll draft the PR today and include a small test harness.
Liam O'Neill: I'll start instrumenting cache invalidation hooks in runtime.
Infra Bot: Assigned: INC-2026-0412 -> owner Maria Chen, sev=trivial (tracking).
Samir Rao: Quick note — let's avoid a blanket opt-out on driver < 536; instead make it conditional on container lib absence. We don't want to lose perf on legitimate H100s.
Maria Chen: Agreed. PR will remove the early-driver-only guard and replace with combined check.
Josh Patel: One more thing: add a per-request warning (sampled) when runtime falls back from bf16 to fp32 so teams see perf impact in trace logs.
Anya Singh: +1. That will help link customer-side perf regressions to our kernel chooser.
Maria Chen: Thanks all — will ping thread with PR link and perf numbers once ready. :rocket:
